- **self**: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments (9/3)

## How it works

- [statement] A query predicate using $elemMatch on an array of embedded documents selects a parent document only when at least one single array element satisfies every condition inside the operator. A conjunction of dotted-path predicates without $elemMatch can select a parent when different embedded documents satisfy different conditions. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch/ · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-array-of-documents/, https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18335248/dot-notation-vs-elemmatch, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/elemmatch-functionality/100363, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/can-i-use-in-to-match-on-multiple-fields-in-an-array-of-objects/274675
- [statement] For a compound multikey index with keys on sibling subfields of the same array, MongoDB can compound the bounds when $elemMatch is applied at the common array path. Placing $elemMatch at a diverging path does not satisfy this path requirement. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds/ · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-array-of-documents/
- [statement] The query-predicate form of $elemMatch matches a parent document only when the named field is an array with at least one element that satisfies every criterion inside $elemMatch. For an array of subdocuments, all enclosed field predicates must match the same subdocument; a non-array embedded object does not satisfy this array-element condition. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch/ · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-array-of-documents/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A single $ne predicate has different array semantics with and without $elemMatch: $elemMatch with the field's $ne matches when at least one array element differs from the value, while dotted-path $ne matches only when no array element equals the value. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch/ · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments · also: https://www.codeforgeek.com/elemmatch-in-mongodb/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The query-predicate form of $elemMatch filters which parent documents are returned but leaves each matching document's array intact. The separate projection form returns only the first array element that matches its explicit condition. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch/ · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-array-of-documents/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch/
- [statement] For one ordinary positive predicate on a subdocument field, dotted-path syntax can test whether an array element has that value without an explicit $elemMatch. The forms are not universally equivalent: MongoDB's example shows dotted-path syntax also matching a field stored as a non-array embedded object, while $elemMatch matches only arrays. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch/ · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/63301922/elemmatch-works-on-a-normal-field-inside-the-array, https://www.codeforgeek.com/elemmatch-in-mongodb/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-array-of-documents/, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/can-i-use-in-to-match-on-multiple-fields-in-an-array-of-objects/274675
- [statement] Spring Data MongoDB's Criteria.elemMatch(Criteria) and Mongoose's Query.prototype.elemMatch(path, filter) expose builder methods for creating a MongoDB $elemMatch query condition. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/mongodb/reference/api/java/org/springframework/data/mongodb/core/query/Criteria.html · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments · also: https://mongoosejs.com/docs/api/query.html, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch/
- [statement] For multikey indexes, $elemMatch can let MongoDB intersect bounds for predicates on one array field and compound bounds for indexed subfields from the same array. To compound same-array subfield bounds, the indexed paths must share a common path and $elemMatch must target that array path; placing it at a different path does not enable the compounding. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds/ · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments · also: https://www.codeforgeek.com/elemmatch-in-mongodb/
- [statement] Mongoose's query builder exposes the MongoDB $elemMatch predicate through Query.prototype.elemMatch(path, filter) and query.where(path).elemMatch(filter). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://mongoosejs.com/docs/api/query.html · keywords: $elemMatch semantics on arrays of subdocuments
